nodes.label: Assess
nodes.desc: Map skill level per domain on the Dreyfus scale from evidence; pick 3 growth edges.

nodes.label: Reflect
nodes.desc: Project debrief: timeline, designer-tendency audit, outcome vs decision quality.

nodes.label: Lineage
nodes.desc: Trace a design move to its historical roots and original intent; build a study set.

nodes.label: Curriculum
nodes.desc: 4/8/12-week plan: input + application to real work + spaced review, interleaved.

nodes.label: Ingest
nodes.desc: Add a source with the shared schema; update index, log, wiki pages and map.

nodes.label: Query
nodes.desc: Answer from the wiki with citations; file reusable syntheses back as pages.

nodes.label: Lint
nodes.desc: Health-check: contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing links, evidence, name hygiene.

nodes.label: Module S · Safety-critical & HMI
nodes.desc: Situation awareness, human error, automation & trust, alarms, high-performance HMI, remote ops.

nodes.label: Module A · Accessibility & inclusive design
nodes.desc: WCAG 2.2, situational disability, contrast, targets, cognitive & motion, audits, law.

nodes.label: Module T · Design systems & tokens
nodes.desc: DTCG 2025.10, tiers, naming, Figma variables & modes, pipeline, governance, lint/CI, agents.

nodes.label: Module B · Brand identity
nodes.desc: Distinctive assets, brand architecture, identity systems, brand in product UI, mark stress tests.

nodes.label: Module G · Game UX & player psychology
nodes.desc: Hodent, SDT, flow, MDA, HUD taxonomy, onboarding, playtesting, game accessibility.

nodes.label: uxtools Challenges (18)
nodes.desc: Hands-on briefs: Understand, Ideate, Test, Implement.

nodes.label: uxtools Surveys
nodes.desc: 2024 Design Tools Survey (2,220) and 2026 State of Prototyping (1,478).

nodes.label: Karpathy · LLM Wiki
nodes.desc: Raw sources, LLM-maintained wiki, schema; ingest, query, lint; index.md + log.md.

nodes.label: Deliberate practice
nodes.desc: Ericsson et al. 1993: narrow targets, feedback, focused repetition.

nodes.label: Reflective practice
nodes.desc: Schön 1983: reflection in and on action.

nodes.label: Design fixation
nodes.desc: Signal: Concepts all resemble the first reference you looked at. Counter: Diverge *before* looking at references; do 3 intentionally different directions; bring in a distant-domain analogy.

nodes.label: Primary generator / anchoring on first idea
nodes.desc: Signal: Concept 1 survives every round untouched. Counter: "Kill your darling" round: argue for the best alternative.

nodes.label: Einstellung / functional fixedness
nodes.desc: Signal: Reaching for the familiar pattern even when the problem differs. Counter: Re-describe the problem without UI nouns; ask "what would this be if not a screen?".

nodes.label: Law of the Instrument
nodes.desc: Signal: Every problem becomes a component, a modal, a dashboard. Counter: Name the job first (JTBD), then the form.

nodes.label: Curse of knowledge
nodes.desc: Signal: You can't see why users don't "get it"; labels use internal jargon. Counter: Read-aloud test, 5-second test, a novice walkthrough.

nodes.label: False consensus
nodes.desc: Signal: "Users will obviously…" without data. Counter: Write the assumption down as a falsifiable hypothesis.

nodes.label: Confirmation bias in research
nodes.desc: Signal: Interview guide leads; you remember the quotes that agree. Counter: Pre-register what would prove you wrong; have someone else code the notes.

nodes.label: IKEA effect / endowment
nodes.desc: Signal: Over-valuing work you built; defending pixels in critique. Counter: Separate "my work" from "the work"; critique a stranger's version of the same brief.

nodes.label: Sunk cost
nodes.desc: Signal: Continuing a direction because of time spent. Counter: Ask "would I start this today?" at each milestone.

nodes.label: Aesthetic-usability blind spot
nodes.desc: Signal: Beautiful mockups pass critique, fail tests. Counter: Test in greyscale / lo-fi; measure tasks not opinions.

nodes.label: Bandwagon / trend herding
nodes.desc: Signal: Work looks like this year's Dribbble/Mobbin. Counter: LINEAGE mode: trace the trend; borrow intent, not surface.

nodes.label: Survivorship bias in inspiration
nodes.desc: Signal: Studying only polished shots, not failures or constraints. Counter: Study case studies with constraints and post-mortems.

nodes.label: Taste gap
nodes.desc: Signal: Frustration that your work doesn't match your taste. Counter: Normal for growth; volume + iteration closes it.
nodes.grade: Ira Glass; Hack Design "Closing the Creative Gap" · Practitioner

nodes.label: Dunning-Kruger (both directions)
nodes.desc: Signal: Over-confidence in new domains; under-rating mastered ones. Counter: Calibrate with external evidence and critique.

nodes.label: Planning fallacy
nodes.desc: Signal: Design estimates always slip. Counter: Reference-class estimates from past tickets; plan to 70%.

nodes.label: Satisficing too early
nodes.desc: Signal: First workable answer ships. Counter: Set a quality bar up front (D5 principles).

nodes.label: Problem/solution co-evolution ignored
nodes.desc: Signal: Treating the brief as fixed. Counter: Reframe the brief explicitly; designers solve by conjecture (Lawson 1979, Dorst & Cross 2001).

nodes.label: Hindsight bias in retros
nodes.desc: Signal: "We should have known". Counter: Judge decisions by info available then.

nodes.label: Phantom competency
nodes.desc: Signal: AI-assisted output is better than what you could make or critique unaided. Counter: Periodically rebuild key pieces by hand; review AI output against principles you can state.

nodes.label: Artifact = seniority
nodes.desc: Signal: Measuring yourself by output volume or polish. Counter: Shift effort upstream: what should exist, the bar it must meet, what to kill.

nodes.label: Nominal-path bias
nodes.desc: Signal: Specs and tests cover the happy path; emergencies are an afterthought. Counter: Design and test off-nominal scenarios first (Module S).
nodes.grade: Human-factors practice (off-nominal scenario testing, Module S) · Practitioner

nodes.label: Typography
nodes.desc: Gutenberg (c. 1450) → Garamond, Bodoni → Futura (Renner 1927) → Tschichold Die neue Typographie 1928 → Helvetica (Miedinger 1957) → Bringhurst Elements of Typographic Style 1992. Intent: Legibility at scale; modernity; neutral voice

nodes.label: White space
nodes.desc: Japanese Ma (間) and Zen ink painting → Tschichold's asymmetric layout → Swiss International Style. Intent: Emptiness as active form; tension and focus

nodes.label: Grids
nodes.desc: Medieval page canons (Villard de Honnecourt / Van de Graaf) → Bauhaus → Gerstner Designing Programmes 1964 → Vignelli/Unimark (NYC subway 1970) → Müller-Brockmann Grid Systems 1981. Intent: Objective, rational order; programmes not one-offs

nodes.label: Visual hierarchy & composition
nodes.desc: Renaissance perspective (Brunelleschi c. 1415, Alberti De pictura 1435) → chiaroscuro (Caravaggio) → Gestalt (Wertheimer 1923) → Arnheim Art and Visual Perception 1954. Intent: Directing the eye to the story's climax

nodes.label: Colour
nodes.desc: Isaac Newton's Opticks (1704) → Goethe Theory of Colours 1810 → Chevreul simultaneous contrast 1839 → Itten (Bauhaus) → Albers Interaction of Color 1963. Intent: Colour is relative, perceived in context

nodes.label: Icons & pictograms
nodes.desc: Egyptian hieroglyphs → Isotype (Neurath & Arntz, 1920s–30s) → Aicher's Munich 1972 Olympic pictograms → Susan Kare's Macintosh icons 1984. Intent: A universal visual language across languages

nodes.label: Skeuomorphism ↔ flat
nodes.desc: Trompe-l'œil → Arts & Crafts honesty of materials → Bauhaus/Swiss reduction → iOS 6 → iOS 7 (2013). Intent: Familiarity during transition vs honesty to the medium

nodes.label: Super normal / restraint
nodes.desc: Shaker furniture → Mingei (Yanagi, 1920s) → Rams' 10 principles → Fukasawa & Morrison Super Normal 2006. Intent: Beauty of anonymous, well-used everyday objects

nodes.label: Motion
nodes.desc: Muybridge's motion studies 1878 → Futurism (Balla) → Disney's 12 principles (Thomas & Johnston, The Illusion of Life 1981) → Apple fluid interfaces. Intent: Believable life; weight and intent

nodes.label: Depth / 3D
nodes.desc: Linear perspective → stereoscopy (Wheatstone 1838) → Sutherland's Sketchpad 1963 & head-mounted display 1968. Intent: Simulating presence

nodes.label: Data visualisation
nodes.desc: Playfair 1786 → Nightingale 1858 → Minard 1869 → Bertin Semiology of Graphics 1967 → Tufte 1983. Intent: Argument through evidence

nodes.label: Systems & components
nodes.desc: Gerstner's programmes → Unimark manuals → Christopher Alexander A Pattern Language 1977 → Atomic Design (Frost 2013). Intent: Reusable rules that generate many solutions

nodes.label: Human-centred design
nodes.desc: Dreyfuss Designing for People 1955 → Norman The Design of Everyday Things 1988 → IDEO / d.school. Intent: Fit the object to the person

nodes.label: Ethics & responsibility
nodes.desc: Garland's First Things First 1964 (renewed 2000) → Papanek Design for the Real World 1971 → Monteiro → deceptive.design. Intent: Designers are accountable for impact

nodes.label: Behaviour design
nodes.desc: Skinner's reinforcement schedules (1950s) → Fogg's captology (Stanford) → Eyal's Hook. Intent: Shape repeated behaviour

nodes.label: Process & problem framing
nodes.desc: Simon The Sciences of the Artificial 1969 → Rittel & Webber "wicked problems" 1973 → Schön 1983 → Cross Designerly Ways of Knowing 2006. Intent: Design as its own way of knowing

nodes.label: Personal style & authorship
nodes.desc: Arts & Crafts (Morris) vs Modernist anonymity → Paul Rand → Saul Bass → Meg Lewis. Intent: Voice vs neutrality

nodes.label: Learning by copying
nodes.desc: Renaissance workshops; copyists at the Louvre; calligraphy copybooks. Intent: Internalise the master's decisions

nodes.label: Human factors & accidents
nodes.desc: Chapanis & Fitts 1940s, TMI 1979, Therac-25, AF447, 737 MAX (Module S).

nodes.label: Universal & inclusive design
nodes.desc: Curb cuts, Section 508, Mace 1997, WCAG 1999-2023, Microsoft Inclusive 2016 (Module A).

nodes.label: Identity programmes
nodes.desc: Aicher Lufthansa 1962, Rand IBM, C&G, Unimark 1970, NASA 1975, MIT Media Lab 2011 (Module B).

nodes.label: Game design & play
nodes.desc: World 1-1 1985, Bartle 1996, MDA 2004, SDT 2006, Chen 2007, Hodent 2017 (Module G).
